title: Teknaf traffickers lure Rohingya and locals: 92 rescued in 17 days
excerpt: Gangs hold captives in the hills of Hnila and Baharchhara before moving them to boats bound for Malaysia and Thailand. A soldier was killed in a rescue on 5 November.

image.alt: Boats on the Naf river at Teknaf port, Cox's Bazar
image.credit: Anik Sarker / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0

content:
Security forces rescued 92 people in three trafficking-related operations in Teknaf and Cox's Bazar over 17 days, The Daily Star reported on Monday (23 November). The victims include Rohingya refugees and Bangladeshis from Teknaf, Ukhiya and Chakaria.

On 5 November, 56 people were rescued in Nuralipara, Hnila. Soldier Md Titas Sheikh was killed when armed traffickers opened fire, and six suspected brokers were detained. On the night of 20 November, 28 people were rescued from a trawler that ran aground at Laboni Point in Cox's Bazar. Early on 22 November, eight Rohingya, including five women and an eight-month-old baby, were rescued in Teknaf after an army-led operation, according to ISPR.

How the traps work

Survivors described being lured with offers of construction work, a trip to Malaysia or a visit to an acquaintance. They said they were held in guarded houses and hill hideouts in Hnila and Baharchhara, then taken by small boat from Mithapanir Chhara or a Marine Drive beach to trawlers waiting offshore. Rohingya women and unmarried girls are targeted with promises of marriage in Malaysia. Families said brokers demanded ransoms or fares of Tk 1.2 lakh to Tk 5 lakh. The paper said it could not verify some survivor accounts, and police said they would investigate claims that people were thrown into the sea.

Khin Maung, president of the United Council of Rohingya, blamed "unemployment, prolonged displacement, and uncertainty over repatriation" for pushing young people towards the boats.

Why it matters

With rations tight, few jobs and repatriation stalled, protection agencies in the camps expect more attempts at the sea crossing as the dry season begins. Host community families are now caught in the same networks. Counter-trafficking, GBV and community protection programmes in Teknaf and Ukhiya will need to reach both groups.

What to watch

Progress in the case filed over the 20 November rescue, and whether UNHCR and IOM report a rise in boat departures this season.
